subject: Pilot credit escalation: competitive comparison clause and timeboxed extension
messages:
From: Evan Miles <evan@pulsehealth.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@pulsehealth.io>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot request / small bake-off — additional credits needed

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We have a short internal RFP — two vendors (you + one incumbent) — and we want to run a 2-week head-to-head on our core clinical triage flows. The engineering team is asking for a small credit top-up so they can run more realistic batch workloads and simulate 24h traffic.

Can Redwood extend an extra 200k tokens for the trial and keep the trial active for 21 days instead of 14? We’ve seen vendors tie additional credits to non-compete clauses; that’s not acceptable for us — we need a neutral evaluation. Happy to sign a short MOU for the scope.

Attached: pulsehealth-bakeoff-scope.pdf (pdf)

Cheers,
Evan
Evan Miles
Director of Platform Engineering
PulseHealth

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Miles <evan@pulsehealth.io>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request / small bake-off — additional credits needed

Hi Evan — thanks for the scope doc and the clear ask. Short answers: likely yes, with conditions. Longer: our standard eval allowance is 75k tokens for a 14-day pilot. For competitive bake-offs we can provide supplemental credits up to 250k tokens and extend the trial window to 21 days, but we need:

- A short MOU (non-binding) that confirms evaluation criteria and that PulseHealth may evaluate multiple vendors.
- A usage plan (engineers to share test harness + expected traffic profile) so we can provision a temporary quota safely.
- Monitoring and throttles enabled by our DevRel/SE during the test.
- A clause that prevents public benchmarking that attributes results to specific vendors without approval.

I’m looping in Priyom from Partner Sales to confirm the credit accounting and Neha from Ops for the quota exception. If you’re comfortable with the bullets above I’ll escalate for a formal approval and get the paperwork back to you today.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot request / small bake-off — additional credits needed

Priyom / Neha — forwarding PulseHealth request. Key ask: +200k tokens and 7 extra days on top of standard 14 (so 21 total). Attach is their scope. Proposed guardrails: temporary quota, SE monitoring, signed MOU, no public vendor-specific benchmark without consent.

Quick Qs:
- Priyom: will granting 200k (250k total allowance) and extension require a deal credit or can we mark as eval stipend? Any revenue/sales ops flags?
- Neha: will this require an exception on quota provisioning and can ops enable usage throttles and prefix cache limits?

If you both give green I’ll confirm with Pulse and send the MOU. Time-sensitive — they want to start Monday.

Ben — I’m fine with the ask from a commercial standpoint. For competitive bake-offs we typically structure it as an "eval stipend" rather than discounting the deal to avoid accounting issues. I recommend:

- Grant 200k supplemental tokens (bring total to 275k for the pilot)
- Extend the trial to 21 days (start date must be explicit in MOU)
- Require a light MOU: scope + dates + evaluation criteria + confidentiality clause about public benchmarking
- Track usage in HubSpot and mark as "eval-stipend" so Finance can reconcile.

I’ll own the HubSpot update and the internal finance tag. Priyom
Head of Partner Sales (covering enterprise pilots)

Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request / small bake-off — additional credits needed

Evan / Ben — ops side is okay to provision, with a couple operational guardrails from our side:

1) We’ll create a temporary tenant quota for PulseHealth capped at 275,000 tokens for a 21-day window starting on the agreed kickoff date.
2) SE will run churn and burst tests and enable prefix-level throttles to prevent noisy neighbors.
3) We need the signed MOU before provisioning; we can fast-track once we have an agreed PDF.
4) We will instrument a usage dashboard and shared alerting to PulseHealth engineers and Ben.

I’ll attach the internal approval artifact (competitive-credit-approval.pdf) to the HubSpot record and mark the quota exception as approved. Ben — please confirm the start date and get the MOU signed; I’ll schedule the provisioning.

—Neha Kapoor
Head of Technical Operations | Redwood Inference
